# model_rebuild incorrectly determines rebuild not required

### Description

I am encountering a case where `model_rebuild` is not properly resolving a forward reference. 

Specifically, this is when the parent class (`Core`) has a field that contains a forward reference to the child class (`Part`), and the child class has no other forward references. Calling `model_rebuild` on the child class does not give any return value, which from the API docs means that it determined no rebuild was required.

This example was [reported](https://github.com/drivendataorg/erdantic/issues/153) to me by a user of my package that depends on a successful `model_rebuild`. My understanding is that this data structure is useful for implementing trees where you want to distinguish root nodes from children nodes. 

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel

class Core(BaseModel):
    part: list['Part']

class Part(Core):
    pass


# Still forward references
Core.model_fields["part"].annotation
#> list['Part']
Part.model_fields["part"].annotation
#> list['Part']

# Rebuild Core, forward reference resolved
Core.model_rebuild()
#> True
Core.model_fields["part"].annotation
#> list[__reprex__.Part]

# Rebuild Part, nothing happens, still unresolved
Part.model_rebuild()
Part.model_fields["part"].annotation
#> list['Part']
```

## Variants where rebuild works as expected

### Child class has a different forward reference

If the child class has a different field that has a forward reference, then that seems to trigger the rebuild.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel

class Core(BaseModel):
    part: list["Part"]

class Part(Core):
    other: "Other"

class Other(BaseModel):
    i: int

# Still forward references
Core.model_fields["part"].annotation
#> list['Part']
Part.model_fields["part"].annotation
#> list['Part']
Part.model_fields["other"].annotation
#> ForwardRef('Other')

# Rebuild Core, forward reference resolved
Core.model_rebuild()
#> True
Core.model_fields["part"].annotation
#> list[__reprex__.Part]

# Rebuild Part, forward references resolved
Part.model_rebuild()
#> True
Part.model_fields["part"].annotation
#> list[__reprex__.Part]
Part.model_fields["other"].annotation
#> <class '__reprex__.Other'>
```

### Reference is to another third model

If the reference on the parent class is to another third model, the rebuild does seem to successfully trigger.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel

class Core(BaseModel):
    other: "Other"

class Part(Core):
    pass

class Other(BaseModel):
    i: int

# Still forward references
Core.model_fields["other"].annotation
#> ForwardRef('Other')
Part.model_fields["other"].annotation
#> ForwardRef('Other')

# Rebuild Core, forward reference resolved
Core.model_rebuild()
#> True
Core.model_fields["other"].annotation
#> <class '__reprex__.Other'>

# Rebuild Part, forward reference resolved
Part.model_rebuild()
#> True
Part.model_fields["other"].annotation
#> <class '__reprex__.Other'>
```
